read.sections.0.text.source: Borobudur is a Buddhist monument in Central Java, Indonesia. It was built in the 700s and 800s. It has stone terraces, walls carved with pictures, and 72 small stupas, or bell-shaped towers. Each stupa holds a statue of the Buddha. UNESCO explains that its levels follow a Buddhist idea of the universe. Many centuries later, people faced a new question: how should it be conserved? A large restoration ran from 1973 to 1983. Indonesia and UNESCO did the work, with help from other countries. The people who restored Borobudur did not build it. It helps to keep these two times apart.
read.sections.0.text.back: Borobudur is a Buddhist monument in Central Java, Indonesia. This monument was built in the 700s and 800s. It has stone terraces, walls carved with pictures, and 72 small stupas, that is, bell-shaped towers. Each stupa holds a statue of the Buddha. UNESCO explains that its levels follow an idea in Buddhism about the universe. Centuries later, people faced a new question: how should this monument be conserved? A large restoration took place from 1973 to 1983. Indonesia and UNESCO did that work, with help from other countries. The people who restored Borobudur are not the people who built it. It is easier for us to understand if these two times are kept apart.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: Borobudur is a Buddhist temple on the island of Java. People built it more than 1,000 years ago. It has stone steps and walls with carved pictures. At the top are 72 small stone towers. Each one holds a statue of the Buddha. From 1973 to 1983, a big team fixed it. This careful work is called conservation. Indonesia and UNESCO did it together. The team did not build the temple.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Borobudur is a Buddhist temple on the island of Java. People built it more than 1,000 years ago. This temple has stone steps and walls with carved pictures. At its top are 72 small stone towers. Each one holds a statue of the Buddha. From 1973 to 1983, a big team repaired the temple. This careful work is called conservation. Indonesia and UNESCO did it together. That team did not build the temple.
read.sections.0.simpler.note: "temple" for Borobudur is "candi", the word used in Malaysia and Indonesia for such monuments (Candi Borobudur, Candi Bukit Batu Pahat).

read.sections.1.heading.back: An archive made while the work went on

read.sections.1.text.source: An archive is a set of records kept so people can study them later. During the restoration, the team took photos, made drawings and films, and wrote reports. An office at Borobudur keeps them today. Its list counts 71,851 sheets of photos and 6,043 sheets of as-built drawings and maps. An as-built drawing shows what workers found and recorded during the work. It is not a plan from the first builders. A later conservator can compare a photo with a drawing and ask why a repair was made. In 2017, UNESCO gave the archive recognition. That date is about the records, not the monument.
read.sections.1.text.back: An archive is a set of records kept so that people can study them later. During the restoration work, the team took photos, made drawings and films, and wrote reports. An office at Borobudur keeps them today. Its list counts 71,851 sheets of photos and 6,043 sheets of as-built drawings and maps. An as-built drawing shows what the workers found and recorded during the work. This drawing is not a plan from the first builders. A conservator in the future can compare a photo with a drawing and ask why a repair was made. In 2017, UNESCO gave recognition to the archive. That date is about the records, not about the monument.
read.sections.1.text.note: "plan" (a builder's plan) is "pelan", a drawing; in Malaysian Malay "pelan" means a plan drawing, which is the meaning here.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: An archive is a set of records. People keep them to look at later. During the work, the team took photos. They made drawings and wrote notes. There are 71,851 sheets of photos. There are 6,043 sheets of as-built drawings. An as-built drawing shows what the workers found. Later, people can look at a photo and a drawing. They can ask why a part was fixed. In 2017, UNESCO gave the archive recognition. That date is about the records.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: An archive is a set of records. People keep them to be looked at later. During that work, the team took photos. They made drawings and wrote notes. There are 71,851 sheets of photos. There are 6,043 sheets of as-built drawings. An as-built drawing shows what the workers found. Later, people can look at a photo and a drawing. They can ask why a part was repaired. In 2017, UNESCO gave recognition to the archive. That date is about the records.

read.sections.2.text.source: The second picture is a photo taken in 1976 by Gerard Bolla for UNESCO. It records a moment of modern conservation work. Look at what is in the photo, then ask what is outside it. A photo cannot tell us what the first builders planned, or why each repair was chosen. It cannot tell us what Borobudur means to every visitor and worshipper. People can add to the record. In 2019, a show of photos by Suparno opened near Borobudur. He worked at the Borobudur office and was trained to photograph the repairs. His memories can answer questions one photo leaves open.
read.sections.2.text.back: The second picture is a photo taken in 1976 by Gerard Bolla for UNESCO. This photo records a moment in modern conservation work. Look at what is in the photo, then ask what is outside it. A photo cannot tell us what the first builders planned, or why each repair was chosen. The photo cannot tell us what Borobudur means to every visitor and every person who comes to worship. People can add to the record. In 2019, an exhibition of photos by Suparno opened near Borobudur. He worked at the Borobudur office and was trained to take photos of the repair work. His memories can answer questions that one photo does not answer.

sensitiveNotes.0.source: Borobudur is a Buddhist place of worship and pilgrimage today. Use respectful, neutral words ("Many Buddhists ...", "UNESCO explains ..."), never rank beliefs, and never ask learners about their own religion; in Speak, "people who come to worship" is a group to think about, not a question about anyone in the room. Preview the video: by UNESCO's account its narration mentions a volcano and describes a carving of the Buddha being tempted.

educatorNotes.0.source: Aim: learners keep the ancient monument (built 700s–800s), the 1973–1983 restoration and the 2017 Memory of the World recognition apart, and write an accurate, dated caption with two limits. Evidence move: put the three dates in three boxes on the board before learners look at the 1976 photo. A sound answer gives who (Gerard Bolla for UNESCO), when (1976) and what (modern conservation work), then two questions the photo cannot answer.

educatorNotes.1.source: Misconception to address: that a conservation photo is evidence of the ancient construction. Source caveats: the archive's numbers (71,851 photo sheets, 6,043 as-built drawing sheets, 425 project documents) come from Indonesia's nomination form on UNESCO's site; the 2017 date comes from news reports of the recognition, as UNESCO's own archive page could not be opened. UNESCO's listing says the temple was rebuilt in two phases in the 1900s, the second from 1973 to 1983; the lesson covers only the second. The back of the 1976 print (Commons file "PHOTO0000003469 0000") carries UNESCO's own typed caption from that time, a source in itself: it calls the work "in progress" and dates UNESCO's agreement with Indonesia to 12 October 1972. Suparno's 2019 exhibition (Borobudur Conservation Office with UNESCO Jakarta) is reported by The Jakarta Post.
